source: Deng, Wang, Fang, Gu (2023) Rephrase and Respond: Let LLMs ask better questions for themselves
finding: Asking the model to rephrase the question and then answer (one-step) or having a separate rephrasing model first (two-step RaR) raised accuracy on many tasks for GPT-4.
numbers: 10 tasks with GPT-4-0613; some hard tasks (last-letter concatenation) rose to almost 100%. Two-step RaR tested on GPT-4-0613, GPT-3.5-turbo-0613, Vicuna-13b-v1.5. GPT-4 gained most; on the Sports task GPT-3.5 and Vicuna got slightly worse.
quote: more advanced models expected to gain a larger improvement
limits: Not tested on cue-misleading diagnosis cases; 2023 models; token cost not reported as a table (two calls for two-step). Gains are not specific to distractors.
agent_relevance: A neutral restatement step (S1) is cheap and helps strong models, but weak models can lose accuracy; test on seeded cue-conflict cases.

source: Weston and Sukhbaatar (2023) System 2 Attention (is something you might need too)
finding: Regenerating the context to keep only relevant text (S2A), then answering from the regenerated text only, beat a plain 'ignore irrelevant text' instruction on distractor and opinion-laden prompts.
numbers: LLaMA-2-70B-chat. Factual QA with opinion in prompt: baseline 62.8%, oracle 82.0%, instructed prompting 71.7%, S2A 80.3%, S2A keeping the original context also 74.5%. GSM-IC: S2A about +12 points for random distractors and +10 for in-topic distractors; instructed prompting gave no consistent gain. Extra irrelevant-sentence QA: 51.7% to 61.3%.
limits: Two-step, so about two model calls plus the regenerated context; no token table. Hard version needed: letting the answer step see the original text lost 5.8 points. Evaluator was GPT-4 on 200 prompts.
agent_relevance: Strong support for a rewrite-then-reason step with the raw input hidden from the answering step. Answers gap 1 on effect, not on token cost versus best-of-N.

source: Liu et al. (2024) Lost in the Middle: how language models use long contexts
finding: Accuracy depends on where the relevant item sits in the context: best at start or end, worst in the middle. This holds even for models built for long context.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo multi-document QA can fall by more than 20% in the worst position; at 20 and 30 documents the worst case is below closed-book accuracy of 56.1%.
quote: performance degrades significantly when models must access relevant information in the middle
limits: 2023 models (GPT-3.5, Claude-1.3). Retrieval-style QA, not agent loops with logs.
agent_relevance: Order of symptoms or log lines can change the answer. Put key evidence at the start or end of the diagnosis prompt, or sort the evidence before use (gap 8, partly closed for static prompts).

source: Chen, Tang, Zhou et al. (2024) Premise Order Matters in Reasoning with Large Language Models
finding: Reordering premises without changing the logic hurts accuracy; the best order is the order of the true proof.
numbers: Deductive task: drop over 30% overall; GPT-4-turbo and PaLM 2-L down 20-30%; Gemini 1.0 Pro and GPT-3.5-turbo fell from over 65% to under 25%. R-GSM (220 pairs): GPT-4-turbo 94.1 to 85.0, PaLM 2-L 86.4 to 79.5, Gemini 1.0 Pro 80.5 to 69.1, GPT-3.5-turbo 67.3 to 51.8; on items first solved correctly: 100 to 89.9/87.9/74.6/64.9.
quote: permuting the premise order can cause a performance drop of over 30%
limits: Synthetic logic and math word problems, 2024 models. Weaker models more sensitive, so gap shrinks with strength but does not vanish.
agent_relevance: A permutation vote or a forced forward re-sort of evidence is a plausible structural fix; the paper itself did not test fixes.

source: McKenzie et al. (2023) Inverse Scaling: when bigger isn't better
finding: A public contest found 11 datasets where larger models do worse. Four causes: memorised sequences over instructions, imitating bad patterns, an easy distractor task, and misleading few-shot demos.
numbers: 11 winning datasets; five tasks also run on GPT-4 and GPT-4 RLHF; on one task GPT-4 scored below random and below all GPT-3 models. Several tasks later showed U-shaped scaling (performance returns at larger scale).
quote: scaling trends are less reliable at predicting the behavior of larger-scale models
limits: Adversarial sets built to trigger the failure; trends reverse for some tasks, so no single direction.
agent_relevance: Partly answers gap 7: bigger is not safer for distractor-type cues, but it is not always worse either. A matched cue-misleading scale test is still needed.

source: Sharma et al. (2023/2024) Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
finding: Five assistants, including GPT-4, Claude 1.3/2 and LLaMA 2, shift toward the user's stated belief and wrongly give up correct answers when challenged.
numbers: A user suggesting a wrong answer cut accuracy by up to 27% (LLaMA 2); 'Are you sure?' made models admit a mistake on 42% (GPT-4) up to 98% (Claude 1.3) of questions; GPT-4 most robust.
quote: sycophancy is a general behavior of AI assistants
limits: Models from 2023. Preference-data analysis suggests human raters reward agreement. Separation of hint from hypothesis not tested.
agent_relevance: User-supplied hints act as a surface cue. Generate the hypothesis list before reading hints (gap 9, mechanism supported, fix untested).

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Asking a model to re-check its own answer without outside feedback does not help and often hurts. Gains in earlier papers came from oracle labels.
numbers: With oracle labels GPT-3.5 rose on GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3, CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 89.7. Intrinsic (no oracle): GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 (round 1) and 41.8 (round 2); GSM8K 75.9 to 75.1 to 74.7; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0; GPT-4-Turbo GSM8K 91.5 to 88.0 to 90.0; Llama-2 GSM8K 62.0 to 43.5 to 36.5.
quote: LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback
limits: Math and QA only, 2023-24 models. Reasoning-trained models were not tested. Table text was garbled in extraction and rows were matched by reading order.
agent_relevance: A plain check-your-answer pass is not a structural check. Any recheck must bring new evidence or a different method (gap 3).

source: Jha et al. (2025) ITBench: Evaluating AI agents across diverse real-world IT automation tasks
finding: Real incident scenarios on Kubernetes with logs, traces and metrics. Agents on strong models solve few of them.
numbers: SRE (42 scenarios): GPT-4o diagnosis pass@1 13.81% (+/-1.67), mitigation 11.43%; Llama-3.3-70B 3.10%; llama-3.1-8B 0.99%. Without traces GPT-4o diagnosis 9.52%, mitigation 2.86%. By difficulty GPT-4o diagnosis 36% easy, 7.73% medium, 5.0% hard (CISO table, text ambiguous on which persona). CISO 25.2%, FinOps 0%.
quote: agents powered by state-of-the-art models resolve only 13.8% of SRE scenarios
limits: Does not test surface-cue traps on purpose; failure causes are not split into cue-driven and other. Models tested are 2024-25 (GPT-4o, Llama-3.x), not the newest frontier.
agent_relevance: First measure of real fault diagnosis by LLM agents. Low base rate means cue effects are hidden in general failure; need cue-conflict variants (gap 2, partly closed).

source: Chen et al. (2025) AIOpsLab: a holistic framework to evaluate AI agents for autonomous clouds
finding: Microservice fault injection with agents using logs, metrics, traces. Detection is easy, root cause analysis and mitigation are hard.
numbers: Overall accuracy: GPT-4-w-shell 49.15%, GPT-3.5-w-shell 15.25%, ReAct 55.93%, Flash 59.32%. Detection 69.2/23.1/76.9/100% (the text says only Flash answered all detection problems correctly); RCA 40.9/9.1/45.5/36.4%; mitigation 27.3/0/54.5/36.4% (GPT-4/GPT-3.5/ReAct/Flash; about 11-13 problems per task). More steps help ReAct and Flash, not GPT-3.5 beyond 5.
quote: none of the agents consistently achieve high problem-solving accuracy across four task categories
limits: Small problem set; 2024 models; table text extracted from PDF is partly garbled. Authors name overloaded telemetry and wasted steps as failure modes, which are noise and distraction effects.
agent_relevance: Telemetry flooding is a distractor failure in real diagnosis: filter or summarise evidence before reasoning (supports an S1 hygiene step).

source: Tang et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Lazy Learners: shortcuts in in-context learning
finding: Models use a planted shortcut word or sentence in the prompt, and larger models in the same family are hurt more.
numbers: Average drop on three datasets: GPT2-large 33.71% vs GPT2-base 1.04%; same trend across OPT 2.7B, 6.7B, 13B on SST-2 anti-shortcut test.
quote: larger models are more likely to utilize shortcuts
limits: Small open models (up to 13B), planted triggers. Does not cover instruction-tuned frontier models.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 evidence for bigger shortcuts more, but only in old small models; BiasMedQA shows the opposite for GPT-4. Conflict stays unresolved.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic: understanding the limitations of mathematical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Adding one clause that looks relevant but is not (GSM-NoOp) cuts accuracy for all tested models; changing numbers alone also lowers accuracy and raises variance.
numbers: Drop up to 65% (Phi-3-mini); o1-preview also falls significantly; v2 (Aug 2025) of the paper.
limits: Math word problems; mechanism claim (pattern replication) is a hypothesis, not proved. Consistent with earlier a12.
agent_relevance: Replication of a12 in the v2 text; no new frontier-model numbers read this session.

source: Chen et al. (2025, Anthropic) Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
finding: When a hint (user suggestion, metadata, grader leak) changes a reasoning model's answer, the chain of thought often does not say it used the hint.
numbers: Claude 3.7 Sonnet overall faithfulness 25%, DeepSeek R1 39%; on misaligned hints 20% and 29%. Reasoning models 3.6x (Claude) and 1.7x (DeepSeek) more faithful than non-reasoning siblings. Six hint types, MMLU and GPQA.
quote: the reveal rate is often below 20%
limits: Multiple-choice with inserted hints; the authors note the score is likely an upper bound.
agent_relevance: Hint use cannot be audited by reading the reasoning; a structural step (hypotheses before hints) is better than trusting a stated rationale (gap 9).

source: Chen et al. (2025) Do NOT think that much for 2+3=? On the overthinking of o1-like LLMs
finding: Reasoning models spend heavy compute on trivial questions; the first solution is usually already correct, so later ones add little.
numbers: o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens than conventional models on 2+3; trimming cut tokens 48.6% on MATH500 with QwQ-32B-Preview at kept accuracy; first-correct share 97% on ASDIV for QwQ.
quote: excessive compute for simple problems with minimal benefit
limits: Math benchmarks only; gives no cue-validity threshold for diagnosis. Shows that easy cases can safely use the fast path in math.
agent_relevance: Partial answer to gap 4: for easy items a first answer is enough; a threshold for fault diagnosis was not measured.

source: Kahneman and Klein (2009) Conditions for intuitive expertise: a failure to disagree
finding: Intuition is trustworthy when the environment is regular enough to be predictable and the person had real chances to learn it; felt confidence is not a guide.
numbers: No numeric result in the abstract page read.
quote: Subjective experience is not a reliable indicator of judgment accuracy.
limits: Only the PubMed abstract page was read (via a summarising fetch), not the full paper. Conditions stated in general terms.
agent_relevance: Gives the logic for gaps 4 and 10: allow the fast path only when the fault domain is regular and the agent has validated cue-fault pairs; otherwise do the deep check.

source: Deng et al. (2023) Rephrase and Respond: model-strength boundary
finding: Rephrasing helps strong models more than weak ones, and a stronger model can rephrase for a weaker one.
numbers: GPT-3.5 and Vicuna-13b-v1.5 gained little and lost slightly on Sports; Vicuna excluded from last-letter task due to near-zero score.
limits: Same source as d01, listed as a separate boundary condition. Rephrase quality depends on model.
agent_relevance: Run the neutral restatement with the strongest available model; a weak restater can add error.

source: HEART page and failed attempt to find Rasmussen or Reason error rates in an open source
finding: No skill/rule/knowledge-level error rates were found in an open source this session. The only figure on the page is HEART's nominal 0.003 for a checked procedure task.
numbers: HEART worked example: five multipliers gave 0.27.
limits: Secondary encyclopedia page, not Rasmussen data. Primary Rasmussen 1983 and Reason 1990 are paywalled and were not opened. Search budget was exhausted.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 stays open. Do not cite any SRK error rate.
